title: Round 4 / ECDLP-11: geometric mechanism of the Sato–Tate law for twisted Legendre sums
question: Identify the geometric object whose Frobenius traces are the psi-twisted sums sum_Q psi(Q) chi(g(Q)) for g = x and g = y on E/F_p, explain the observed SU(2)-like law for both (including the D=4 case g = y), and give the cheapest decisive numerical check.

claims: Derivation+theorem: sum_Q psi(Q)chi(g(Q)) = -tr(F|H^1) of rank D = #(odd-valuation support) (D=2 for x, D=4 for y), weight 1; |S|<=D sqrt(p).

Derivation, numerically verified (14 curves, F_p..F_p^3): for g=x the sum is the trace on the rank-2 H^1(D,pi^*L_psi), D: w^2=x(Q) genus 2, Jac D ~ E x E'' with E'': Y^2=X^3+aX^2+b^2; psi trivial gives -a(E'')-1 exactly (120/120); Newton rank-2 relation and det=p exactly, i.e. SU(2).
Derivation (verified): g=y satisfies S(psi)=chi(-1)conj S(psi): Y real for p=1 mod 4, imaginary for p=3 mod 4; max|Y|<=1.9997 on 120 curves.

Derivation sketch / conjecture: for g=y, H^1 (dim 4)= W(x)M with W the Heisenberg rep of E[2]; Frobenius cycles the T_i so tr_W has modulus 1, giving SU(2)-like law despite D=4. Test S3=A^3-3AB, |A^2-B|/2=p holds exactly on 24 curves (S1..S3 only; not a proof). Control: #E=2r, chi(-B)=-1 gives sums exactly 0 (22/22), chi(-B)=+1 gives max|Y|=2.82.

Conjecture (open): semicircle equidistribution over psi as p->infinity; no verified theorem covers it (FFK framework is the candidate; big-monodromy not verified). No information on discrete logarithms.
